site.name: tablerose
site.summary: tablerose-clone Fictional restaurant reservation platform "Tablerose" multi-page booking flow. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Discovery: hero with 5-field search card (city autocomplete / party / date / time); 5 quick-pill suggestions; 6-card "reserved most this week" trending grid; 4-card editor guides; 3-step "how it works" | | `restaurants.html` | Results: top reservation summary bar with Edit; left filter rail (8 cuisines, 4 price tiers, 6 neighborhoods, 6 features); 10-row results list with photo / name / stars / blurb / tags / per-row time slots (slots within ±30min of search are highlighted, others muted); sort dropdown (relevance / rating / price / distance) | | `restaurant.html` | Detail: split hero (photo / info with stars / dress / hours); 4 tabs (Overview with about, highlights table; Menu with 3 sections; Photos with 9 swatches; Reviews with rating bars + 3 reviews); right-side sticky booking card (date / party / 10 time slots — 30min near target highlighted, 17:00/21:30 disabled for Bella Suora); SVG mini-map; favorite heart toggle |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full tablerose system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Tablerose booking flow functions logically but suffers from severe mobile usability issues, particularly regarding touch target sizes and layout stability. Critical post-booking actions (Modify/Cancel) are non-functional placeholders, creating a trust gap for users needing to change plans. Additionally, the interface lacks necessary accessibility labels for form controls and exhibits horizontal overflow on mobile viewports.

exploration_plan.goal: Execute a comprehensive UX audit of the Tablerose reservation flow, validating the end-to-end booking journey from discovery to confirmation, while identifying usability friction points and mobile responsiveness issues.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will simulate a user booking a table at 'Bella Suora' for a party of 2. It begins with search validation on the homepage, moves through filtering and selection on the results page, inspects details on the restaurant page, and completes the multi-step checkout (Guest Info -> Payment -> Confirmation). Finally, it will repeat critical path checks on a mobile viewport to address known tap-target risks.
assumptions: The site is a static prototype; form submissions will navigate to hardcoded next steps rather than processing real payments.
'Bella Suora' is the primary test case as it appears in trending lists and has specific disabled slot logic mentioned in the prescan.
The '9+ guests' option may trigger different UI states or warnings compared to standard parties.
risk_hotspots: Mobile navigation bar (known small tap targets < 44px)
Restaurant detail page sticky booking card (interaction with disabled slots like 17:00/21:30)
Payment page add-ons (checking if selecting items updates the total correctly)
Filter rail on restaurants.html (usability of dense checkbox lists on mobile)

phases.title: Discovery & Search Validation
phases.objective: Validate the entry point, search widget functionality, and quick-link navigation.
key_checks: Verify 'Find tables' button triggers navigation to results.
Test 'Party' dropdown including edge case '9+ (request)'.
Click 'Pasta' quick pill to verify filtered results load.
Check layout stability of the hero section.
exit_criteria: Successfully navigated to restaurants.html via both main search and quick pills.

phases.title: Results & Filtering
phases.objective: Assess the usability of the filter rail and result cards.
key_checks: Apply multiple filters (e.g., Italian + $$$) and observe list updates.
Test 'Sort' dropdown functionality.
Verify 'Edit' link in the top summary bar returns to search state.
Select 'Bella Suora' from the list.
exit_criteria: Filters applied successfully; navigated to restaurant.html.

phases.title: Restaurant Detail Inspection
phases.objective: Evaluate information architecture and the sticky booking widget.
key_checks: Toggle tabs: Overview, Menu, Photos, Reviews.
Interact with the sticky booking card: change date/party size.
Attempt to select a disabled time slot (e.g., 17:00 or 21:30) to check error handling.
Click 'Favorite' heart toggle.
exit_criteria: All tabs viewed; valid time slot selected; navigated to guest.html.

phases.title: Checkout Flow Execution
phases.objective: Complete the reservation transaction and validate form UX.
key_checks: Fill Guest Details: Test dietary restriction checkboxes and special request char limit.
Payment Page: Select an add-on (e.g., Cake +$8) and verify total updates.
Submit 'Hold the table' and verify transition to Confirmation.
On Confirmation: Check 'Add to calendar' buttons and 'Modify/Cancel' links.
exit_criteria: Full booking completed; confirmation details visible.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness Audit
phases.objective: Re-validate critical flows on mobile viewport to catch layout breaks.
key_checks: Check header nav collapse/hamburger menu behavior.
Verify filter rail on results page becomes a modal or drawer.
Ensure sticky booking card on detail page does not obscure content.
Measure tap targets for 'Sign In' and 'Discover' against 44px standard.

coverage_targets.features: All form inputs, dropdowns, and filter checkboxes exercised at least once
coverage_targets.mobile: Primary booking flow repeated on iPhone SE/12 viewport

notes: Pay close attention to the 'Payment' page logic regarding the $50 no-show fee explanation vs the actual card hold amount.
The prescan indicates 'small_tap_target' warnings on almost all nav items; document these specifically in Phase 5.

findings.user_goal: Filter restaurants and select time slots on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Interactive elements are significantly smaller than the recommended 44x44px minimum, making them difficult to tap accurately.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flag filter checkboxes at 13x13px, navigation links <44px height, and time slot buttons at 96x31px. The 'Edit' button on the results page is only 25x16px.
findings.why_it_matters: Users on mobile devices will experience high friction and error rates when trying to refine searches or book tables, leading to frustration and potential abandonment.
findings.suggestion: Increase padding and dimensions for all interactive elements. Specifically, expand filter checkboxes to at least 44x44px hit areas and ensure time slot buttons have sufficient vertical height.
findings.source_hint: restaurants.html: Filter rail checkboxes; restaurant.html: Time slot grid

findings.user_goal: Modify or cancel a reservation after booking.
findings.problem: The 'Modify' and 'Cancel' buttons on the confirmation page are non-functional placeholders that provide no feedback or navigation.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Modify' (ux-7) and 'Cancel' (ux-8) resulted in no URL change, modal appearance, or state update. The 'Help' link also fails to open any resource.
findings.why_it_matters: This creates a significant trust gap. Users need confidence that they can rectify mistakes or change plans. Dead ends in critical recovery paths make the application feel broken or untrustworthy.
findings.suggestion: Implement functional modals or navigation flows for modifying/canceling bookings. If these features are out of scope, clearly disable the buttons or provide a 'Contact Support' alternative.

findings.user_goal: Select party size using screen reader assistance or clear visual cues.
findings.problem: The party size selector lacks an associated label, aria-label, or placeholder text.
findings.evidence: Observation notes on `restaurant.html` and `index.html` identify the `<select>` element for party size as having no accessible name. It relies solely on visual proximity to the 'Party' header.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will hear 'combo box' or similar generic terms without context, making it unclear what the control does. This violates WCAG guidelines for form labeling.
findings.suggestion: Add an `aria-label='Party Size'` or visually hidden `<label>` element to the party size dropdown.

findings.user_goal: View content without horizontal scrolling on mobile.
findings.problem: The page width exceeds the viewport width, causing horizontal overflow.
findings.evidence: Layout warning on `restaurant.html` (mobile viewport) states: 'Page width 396px exceeds viewport 390px'.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal scrolling disrupts the natural vertical reading flow of mobile web pages and often indicates layout bugs or uncontained elements, degrading the perceived quality of the site.
findings.suggestion: Inspect CSS for fixed-width elements or margins that push content beyond the viewport boundary and ensure `box-sizing: border-box` is applied globally.

findings.user_goal: Receive confirmation that an action (like resending email) was successful.
findings.problem: Action buttons like 'Resend email' and calendar exports provide no visible system status feedback.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Resend email' (ux-6) and 'Google' calendar export (ux-4) produced no toast message, modal, or text change, leaving the user unsure if the action occurred.
findings.why_it_matters: Lack of feedback violates the 'Visibility of System Status' heuristic. Users may repeatedly click the button, thinking it failed, or assume the feature is broken.
findings.suggestion: Implement immediate visual feedback, such as a temporary success toast notification or a disabled state with a checkmark, upon clicking these actions.
